claim: See-through glasses project imagery directly onto retinas.
originalWording: See-through glasses project imagery directly onto retinas.

sources.title: How My Predictions Are Faring — Ray Kurzweil
sources.locator: The Computer Itself, prediction 17, printed p. 25

sourceCaveat: The original book edition has not been independently checked. See the listed source and full record for attribution limits.

reference.criterion: Practical see-through head-worn displays project imagery onto the retina and are used, without a mass-adoption requirement.
reference.rationale: Microvision’s Nomad retinal display was deployed in a dealership in 2004, establishing practical use before 2009. This is a capability/use success, even though the product was specialized rather than popular fashion eyewear.

evidence.title: Microvision: Nomad retinal display installed at Chevrolet dealership
evidence.note: Microvision-issued release hosted by The Auto Channel: actual industrial deployment. strict.criterion: The retinal display is built into ordinary eyeglass-form eyewear rather than a headband/industrial head-mounted unit.
strict.rationale: The located deployment is materially similar optical technology but not the exact eyeglass form. The strict mechanical-form reading remains partial.
